title: Antenna: two-week OKR scout log
body:
Purpose: micro-scout cadence to detect signal early in the two-week OKR rhythm. This is a light-weight scratchpad — not a final retro. Use it to capture hunches, quick experiments, and whether the signals justify a course-correction before the formal OKR review.

Snapshot (week 1->2):
- Focus objective: O1 (reduce inferencing unit cost per 1k tokens for hosted-api by 12% through batching + cache tweaks).
- Key personal results I’m tracking this sprint: KR1: run 3 batching experiments with traffic simulator; KR2: draft rollout plan for canary config; KR3: ship one dashboard widget for token-level cost attribution (MVP).
- Quick score (0-10) how I feel about progress: 5 -> uneven velocity; experiments ran but integration stalled.

What happened (notes to self):
- Monday: sketched batching matrix (sequence lengths x batch size x latency tail). Shorthand notes in the simulator notebook (see linked artifact).
- Tuesday: pairing session with Eliot to port kernel selection heuristics into the simulator; got preliminary variance numbers. Good early signal: 8% median cost reduction in synthetic workload A, 4% in workload B.
- Wednesday: discovered a cache invalidation edge case when using prefix caching with streaming; had to pause test harness. Filed RDI-3421 (linked).
- Thursday: spent too long on dashboard auth plumbing; estimate mismatch — should have been 2h but took half-day. Need to log time estimate bias.
- Friday: quick demo to Marta; feedback: need per-route breakouts and a toggle to compare baseline vs. candidate easily.

Hypotheses & micro-experiments (what I set up):
- H1: Increasing batch size for short seqs (<=64) reduces cost 10–15% without breaking 95th pct latency SLO. Experiment: run production-shaped traffic replay with batch sizes 4,8,16. Status: completed for batch 4/8. Observations: median cost down 7% for batch8; 95th pct latency increased by 40ms -> acceptable for background routes, not for interactive.
- H2: KV prefix caching will reduce repeated-prefix token cost for chat flows by 20%. Experiment paused due to cache invalidation bug. Next step: reproduce minimal repro and add unit test.
- H3 (personal process): Pairing on integration tasks reduces context-switch time and unblock rate. Tracked via calendar blocks and PR cycle time: two pairing blocks this week correlated with 1.3x faster PR merge for paired tasks.

Signals worth attention (early decision points):
- If batch8 benefits continue on real traffic and 95th pct stays within +50ms, promote to canary for background cohort (10% traffic).
- Cache bug is highest risk for KR2 timeline; raise blocking flag if not resolved by end of next sprint.

Retrospective snippets (what felt off / what worked):
- Off: over-ambitious scope for dashboard work; under-accounted for infra auth complexity. Action: break dashboard into tiny verticals next sprint.
- Off: switching between simulation code and product auth created cognitive overhead. Action: allocate two dedicated dev blocks per week for simulation-only time.
- Worked: pairing with Eliot accelerated tricky kernel assumptions; keep pairing for cross-domain technical lift.

Concrete action items (two-week plan):
- A1: Reproduce cache invalidation in unit test environment and attach minimal failing test to RDI-3421 (owner: Noor) — estimate 6h — due: 2026-03-05.
- A2: Finish batch8/16 replay on production traffic mirror for the next 48h window, grab p50/p95/p99 cost and latency. If p95 < baseline+50ms, prepare canary rollout notes (owner: Noor + SRE) — estimate 12h — due: 2026-03-07.
- A3: Dashboard MVP: create per-route toggle for baseline vs candidate and wire up a lightweight sample dataset; postpone auth integration until after MVP demo (owner: Noor) — estimate 10h — due: 2026-03-10.
- A4: Time-estimate calibration: keep a log of actual vs estimated hours for each task this sprint; review on Friday and adjust future estimates.

Metrics tracker (how I’ll know we moved the needle):
- Unit cost per 1k tokens (tracked in dashboard) — target -12% vs baseline.
- 95th pct latency change — must stay < +50ms for interactive routes.
- PR cycle time for paired tasks vs solo — aim for 1.25x improvement.
- Number of blocking incidents (cache invalidation, auth) — target 0 for next sprint.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Does our production traffic mirror adequately surface the diverse chat-primer prefix shapes? Might need a longer replay window.
- Stakeholder alignment: do Product and Support accept +30–50ms p95 bump for background routes in exchange for cost wins? Need a short doc for product to sign off.
- If cache fix requires schema migration, timeline balloons — contingency plan? Talk to infra about a fast rollback strategy.

Quick wins and experiments to deprioritize:
- Deprioritize: pretty charts and deep RBAC for the dashboard this sprint. MVP first.
- Quick win: add a small sampling flag on the simulator to accelerate runs by 2x (low risk) — aim to do this Thursday.

Notes-to-self (style and cadence reminders):
- Keep these scout logs terse: 3–5 signal lines + 2 actions per week.
- Use this doc to surface blockers early to Marta in weekly sync.
- At formal OKR review, convert this into a 1‑page bullet for KR status.

Scratch alpha snippets (copy-paste ready):
- "Batch8 shows promise: median cost -7% (workload A), p95 +40ms — candidate for background canary if stable across mirror replay."
- "Cache invalidation repro: occurs when prefix length > 128 and streaming enabled. Suspect race in KV eviction path."

End-of-sprint quick log (to paste into formal OKR doc):
- KR1: 2/3 experiments completed; preliminary cost reduction observed (-7% median on batch8).
- KR2: blocked (cache invalidation) — tracking RDI-3421, blocker escalated.
- KR3: Dashboard MVP started, auth postponed; demo scheduled next Friday.

TODO (small checklist):
- [ ] attach failing test to RDI-3421
- [ ] schedule canary kick-off if replay p95 within tolerance
- [ ] demo dashboard MVP to Marta next Friday
- [ ] time-estimate review Friday 4pm

Random brain dump (if I get stuck):
- Could we run an A/B where background cohort uses aggressive batch config + longer timeout and interactive routes remain conservative? Boundary conditions may be product acceptable.
- Consider a 2-stage cache warmup in canary to reduce invalidation surface area.

End.
